meta.title: NOURRA.AI | GPU compute, data centre capacity and delivery in Southeast Asia
meta.description: NOURRA, based in Singapore, verifies and assembles GPU leasing and server procurement, AI data centre colocation in Southeast Asia, fit-out and operations, and enterprise cloud for AI teams and data centre projects.

h1: assembled into compute that goes live.
hero.lede: NOURRA works from Singapore for AI teams and data centre projects that need compute outside mainland China. We verify what each supplier actually has, then assemble it into a plan you can sign and take delivery of.
hero.secondary: See the two ways we work
hero.note: We don’t own GPUs or data centres. A resource we haven’t re-checked in two weeks doesn’t get quoted.

diagram.aria: Diagram: GPU supply, sites and power, fit-out, and cloud and API are each verified, brought together by NOURRA into one deal, and delivered as a running cluster.

problems.title: Four places a compute deal usually gets stuck

items.q: Plenty of quotes, no way to tell which are real
items.d: The same batch gets relayed through several people. Stock on hand, future allocations and units already sold all look alike.
items.a: We grade every resource by how well it’s verified and only quote what we’ve checked recently.

items.q: GPUs without a rack, racks without power
items.d: Servers, rack space, power and network sit with different parties. One missing piece keeps the cluster dark.
items.a: We line up arrival dates, rack positions and power-on dates in one schedule before anyone signs.

items.d: A middleman takes the order without supply behind it, and you find out a month or two later.
items.a: Our quote states the supply status, the delivery conditions, and what happens if delivery fails.

items.q: Compliance questions surface at the last step
items.d: Nobody pinned down the end user or location, and the supplier or data centre stops the deal before delivery.
items.a: We confirm end user, location and use in writing first. Requests that don’t pass, we don’t take.

services.title: Four services, used alone or joined into one deal

items.name: GPU leasing and server procurement
items.fit: AI companies, listed companies and research teams that need whole servers or clusters, deployed outside mainland China.
do: Match lease or purchase supply to your model, quantity, term and delivery location
Verify whether supply is on hand or a future allocation, and the real lead time
Help settle term, prepayment and delivery conditions
items.get: A written quote stating supply status, commercial terms, delivery date and validity.

items.name: AI data centre colocation and development
items.fit: Teams with their own hardware looking for rack space, and developers or investors building AI data centres in Southeast Asia.
do: Source rack space, power and liquid-cooling capacity around Singapore, currently mainly Malaysia and Batam, Indonesia
Check power capacity, permit status and power-on dates
Connect data centre projects with colocation customers, contractors and operators
items.get: A side-by-side sheet of rack and power options, with power-on dates and billing start.

items.name: Fit-out and operations
items.fit: Data centre owners, main contractors and hardware owners that need local crews and on-site staff.
do: Server racking and data centre relocation
Ongoing operations under an agreed SLA
For high-density liquid cooling and GPU cluster networking we bring in a specialist team per project and name who is responsible
items.get: An itemised scope, schedule and operations SLA, carried out by local engineering teams we work with long term.

items.name: Enterprise cloud and model APIs
items.fit: Companies with significant monthly cloud spend, and AI application teams calling large models through public cloud.
do: Set up enterprise accounts, discounts and billing on major public clouds through authorised resellers
Help you enable model APIs properly on those cloud platforms
Only for a company’s own normal usage; model services are available only where their providers support them
items.get: A discount proposal and a clear billing structure.

modes.title: Two ways to work with us, agreed before you sign
modes.intro: The difference is who your contract is with and who is responsible for delivery. Before each deal starts we state in writing which one applies and where our fee comes from.

items.name: Introduction
items.lead: We verify and introduce the right supplier. You contract with the supplier directly.
items.duty: Scope the requirement, verify resources, coordinate terms
items.fit: You need one kind of resource, or already have a procurement process
items.fee: Who pays our service fee and how it’s calculated is stated in writing before the introduction

items.name: NOURRA as contracting party
items.lead: You sign one contract with NOURRA. We organise supply, site, fit-out and operations.
items.duty: Deliver the scope and dates set in the contract
items.fit: Several resources must line up in time and you want one accountable party
items.fee: Contract price and payment milestones are set in the contract

process.title: From first conversation to a running cluster

steps.d: Model or compute size, quantity, location, target go-live date, lease or buy.
Written confirmation of who will use it, where, and for what. If this step fails, we stop here.
We check supply, rack space, power and crew availability one by one and grade each.
A written quote with validity, delivery conditions and which of the two models applies.
Arrival, racking, commissioning and power-on, accepted against contract milestones.
Operations under the SLA. Before the term ends we agree renewal, expansion or exit.

trust.title: The rules we apply to every deal
trust.intro: We don’t yet have client work we can name publicly. These are the rules we follow on every deal, and you can check each one as we work together.

ladder.title: Every resource gets one of four grades. Only the top two are quoted
ladder.note: Any resource not re-checked within two weeks drops out of our quotes.

rules.d: For GPU requests we confirm end user, location and use in writing before discussing supply.
On every deal we state whether we are introducing or contracting, and where our fee comes from.
Supply status, delivery dates and what happens on non-delivery go into the quote and the contract.

wont: Supply or tranship to countries, regions or end users restricted by export controls
Act as a nominee buyer or contracting party on someone else’s behalf
Support model distillation, resale of personal subscriptions, or gambling businesses

team.title: Team
team.text: [To add: publishable background of the founding team and partners]

items.a: There’s no fixed threshold. The smallest workable size depends on the specific supply and site, and suppliers usually prioritise whole batches and longer terms. Tell us the quantity and we’ll say plainly whether it can be done.
It depends on whether supply is on hand or a future allocation, and when the site powers on. The quote gives a date for each stage. We don’t make blanket promises.

items.q: Why are there no prices on this site?
items.a: GPU lease and server prices move quickly with the market, term, prepayment and quantity. A published number is stale within days. We quote in writing against your conditions, with a validity date.

items.q: Does NOURRA own GPUs or data centres?
items.a: No. We assemble verified third-party resources. When NOURRA is the contracting party, NOURRA is responsible to you for delivery.

items.q: Can equipment be shipped to mainland China or other controlled destinations?
items.a: No. We only serve requirements used lawfully in permitted locations, and we confirm end user and location in writing.
For introductions we charge a service fee. Who pays it and how it’s calculated is stated in writing beforehand. When NOURRA is the contracting party, our fee is part of the contract price.
